prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed bifunctional small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to eliminate a chosen protein

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep targeted protein degradation as a single-part prize. The scientific case is unchanged and was not challenged by anyone: a designed molecule that brings a chosen protein to an E3 ligase converts binding into elimination, works on targets without a druggable active site, and has been reproduced by many independent groups. What the exchange sharpened is the credit. The disputed question is whether glues belong in the same citation. I think a citation on rational bifunctional degraders is one coherent achievement with a defensible trio: Crews and Deshaies for the concept and first proof of principle, and Ciulli for structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex cooperativity, which turned the idea into a design discipline. Four members prefer B011 and all eight list it as a preference or alternative, which I treat as a modest sign of robustness and not as a substitute for the scientific argument.
statement.case_against: No degrader is yet a broadly approved drug and I have not verified current trial outcomes, so the committee can fairly say the prize is a few years early. The three-name cap also leaves out Sakamoto and Kim from the 2001 paper, and, under a PROTAC-only citation, Handa, Ito and Gray from the molecular-glue strand, which is a real loss of credit for an established mechanism (cereblon as the thalidomide target). That is the best argument against my configuration and I do not think it can be fully answered.

responses.point: Chabes keeps Handa in the trio and words the citation to cover molecular glues, but says he would accept Ciulli in the third seat if the majority wants a PROTAC-centred prize that does not claim glues.
responses.response: I am grateful for that flexibility and it is where I land: the strongest version of B011 is the narrow one. Handa's identification of cereblon is a landmark of mechanism, but it explains how an existing drug acts, whereas Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli describe designing new degraders. A mixed citation naming glues but crediting only one glue scientist is the least defensible outcome, because Ito and Gray would be omitted in a way the text invites criticism for. I therefore hold Ciulli, and I would word the citation so it does not claim the glue strand. If the committee wants glues honoured I still think that deserves its own treatment, but B011 is the only shortlisted item that carries both strands and I do not see a second distinct shortlisted part for it.

responses.point: Somfai now says genetic code expansion (B042) is mature and chemically inventive, and that he finds it easier to defend than B011 on maturity and attribution if the committee wants a chemical biology prize.
responses.response: You moved me on this: I replace B052 with B042 as my second alternative. Orthogonal tRNA-synthetase pairs gave chemists direct control over protein composition, and thirty years of use is a stronger maturity record than degraders have. But I would still rank B011 above it. The principle in B042 is largely engineering of translation machinery, as you say, and the Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl, Yokoyama split looks harder to settle in three names than Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. On the chair's question: if no degrader is approved by the announcement, I still hold first place, because our criterion is the chemistry's importance and the principle is already confirmed. You would be right that B042 is the safer pick on maturity.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers Gray and Winkler (B058) for a mature, physically stated mechanism, but concedes that priority overlaps with Marcus, Dutton, Moser, Beratan and Onuchic, and that B011 has much broader support.
responses.response: I agree that the physical content of B058 is unusually clear and that four decades of confirmation is a real strength; as someone who builds on protein electron transfer in biosensing, I find it convincing as science. My difficulty is the same one you name: the citation has to be narrowed to the experimental demonstration in proteins to avoid Marcus's 1992 prize, and then it is a prize for confirming a principle already honoured. B011 is a new capability, since it lets chemists and clinicians remove proteins they could not inhibit. I would ask whether you would move to B011 if B058 cannot reach five votes, since your own alternatives list includes it.

responses.point: Sparr concedes that in-cell evidence for phase separation is partly indirect, that Pappu and Mittag are unresolved within three names, and lists B011 as her first alternative.
responses.response: I accept your correction that the purified-protein and P-granule core is better quantified than I credited, and the polymer-physics description by Rosen's multivalent systems is a real strength. My remaining difficulty is not that core but the three-name cap, where Pappu and Mittag are central to the sequence grammar. That would leave the credit as contested as the degrader case, with less evidence of consequences. Since you list B011 as an alternative, I would welcome your view on whether Ciulli's cooperativity work is a physical-chemical result you could support in the citation.

uncertainties: Whether the lack of an approved degrader by the announcement makes the prize premature; I have not verified trial outcomes.
Whether a PROTAC-only citation that omits Handa, Ito, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim will be accepted by members who see the glue and 2001 strands as central.
Whether B042 would be the safer pick on maturity and attribution than B011 for a chemical biology prize.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate. My postdoc mentors (Stevens, Boey) and my peptide-nanoparticle biosensor work do not connect to any named candidate; I share research interests with Emma Sparr in self-assembly, which is not a conflict. Unchanged from round 1.
